gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 368,259,604,498 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD x 0.8005) / population 10,804,871 = 34,083. Range +/-10%. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 460,036,982,508 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 368,259,604,498 2011 int$. Range +/-10% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS: 1.71% of GDP in 2025 (mid), 1.44% in 2024, 1.52% in 2021. Low is the lowest of those years; high allows ~5% for NATO-definition spending above SIPRI.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction 18.3% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-1.5 pp for year-to-year variation.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.1 -> 0.94. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/PRT/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 2.78% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.44 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.42-0.45). Mid 1 - 0.028/0.44 = 0.94. Low: a x 1.5 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.42 = 0.9. High: s 0.45 = 0.94. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 44% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Net food importer (cereals), exporter of wine, fish products.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 5,145,857 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share of males aged 15-19 5.300% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 54,549. Males only (conscript-pool convention); about double if women are counted. Range +/-10%.

ships_minor.note: Educated guess. West Sea Viana do Castelo builds OPVs.

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Portugal is not in the fetched road-network table; analogy to Spain's road density scaled by area. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_countries_by_road_network_size)

railKm.note: asOf 2021: 2,527 route-km (IS.RRS.TOTL.KM). Low allows for closures since.

merchantTonnage.note: UNCTAD 2025 as quoted: 35,943 thousand DWT, inflated by the Madeira international open register (MAR, a flag of convenience); Portuguese-owned tonnage is a small fraction.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. By analogy to NATO mechanized brigade sustainment (truck-based, depots every ~150-200 km).

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, mules and donkeys, not from FAO data. Militarily irrelevant in 2026.

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 lists only nine nuclear-armed states.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1: familiar hilly terrain and local supply; small depth.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data with an Oct 2026 order of battle. Population convention: mainland Portugal plus Azores and Madeira inside ne:PRT. Money in 2011 int$ via derived:ppp-rebase-2011. Merchant tonnage is flag-of-registry (MAR open register). Road length not in the fetched table (grade D). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). GNR excluded.
